pr.title: Fix NPE when accessing group concurrently

raw_findings.body: The method returns null even though the GroupModel interface Javadoc explicitly states getSubGroupsCount() "Never returns null". Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount propagate a null subGroupCount into admin REST responses, and any current or future caller that unboxes the Long (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) throws NullPointerException, reintroducing the class of failure this patch aims to fix.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Interface contract violation that shifts a possible NullPointerException from this adapter into every unboxing caller and emits null counts in API responses.
raw_findings.impact: The method returns null even though the GroupModel interface Javadoc explicitly states getSubGroupsCount() "Never returns null". Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount propagate a null subGroupCount into admin REST responses, and any current or future caller that unboxes the Long (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) throws NullPointerException, reintroducing the class of failure this patch aims to fix.
raw_findings.root_cause: The NPE guard was implemented by returning null on a deleted group instead of a contract-compliant default value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return 0L instead of null when the underlying model is gone (the group was deleted, so it has zero subgroups), keeping the documented non-null contract intact.
raw_findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() may return null, violating GroupModel contract that it never returns null
raw_findings.trigger: A cached group is removed concurrently by another thread/session, so modelSupplier.get() (delegate getGroupById) returns null while another request calls getSubGroupsCount() on the stale GroupAdapter.

raw_findings.body: The exception is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the regression test can report success even when the concurrent read actually failed with the NPE it is designed to detect, making the test unreliable as a guard for issue #40368.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Race between the assertion in the main thread and exception collection in the reader thread yields false-passing test runs.
raw_findings.impact: The exception is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed, so the regression test can report success even when the concurrent read actually failed with the NPE it is designed to detect, making the test unreliable as a guard for issue #40368.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test starts a background thread with new Thread(...).start() but discards the reference and never synchronizes on its completion before verifying results.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a reference to the Thread, call deletedAll.set(true), then thread.join() (with a timeout) before asserting that caughtExceptions is empty.
raw_findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting caughtExceptions, so in-flight failures can be missed
raw_findings.trigger: The reader thread starts a groups() request just before the main thread finishes deletions; the main thread sets deletedAll and immediately runs the assertion while that request is still executing and about to throw.

raw_findings.body: The typo 'groupUuuids' degrades readability and invites copy-paste of the misspelling; it does not match the intended 'groupUuids'/'groupIds' naming used elsewhere in the codebase.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability defect: inconsistent, misspelled identifier reduces code clarity in the new test.
raw_findings.impact: The typo 'groupUuuids' degrades readability and invites copy-paste of the misspelling; it does not match the intended 'groupUuids'/'groupIds' naming used elsewhere in the codebase.
raw_findings.root_cause: Typographical error introduced when naming the new local variable in the added test.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the variable to 'groupUuids' (or 'groupIds') at the declaration and both usages.
raw_findings.title: Misspelled variable name 'groupUuuids' (triple 'u') in new test
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer reading or extending createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti encounters the misspelled identifier used at declaration and at both usage sites (add and forEach).

finding.verifier_reason: The patch at line 275 explicitly introduces `return model == null ? null : model.getSubGroupsCount();`. The GroupModel interface Javadoc at line 296 states 'Never returns null'. Callers like GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount (line 90) pass this directly to setSubGroupCount, propagating null to API responses. Any caller unboxing the Long will get NPE. The trigger (concurrent group deletion causing modelSupplier.get() to return null) is realistic given the caching architecture shown.

finding.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting caughtExceptions, so in-flight failures can be missed
finding.trigger: The reader thread starts a groups() request just before the main thread finishes deletions; the main thread sets deletedAll and immediately runs the assertion while that request is still executing and about to throw.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows the test starts a thread with `.start()` at line 149, then immediately proceeds to delete groups and call `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155, followed by `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` at line 157. There is no join() or synchronization before the assertion. If the reader thread catches an exception after the assertion runs but before the thread terminates, the test passes incorrectly. This is a real race condition in the test design.
